verses.gurmukhi: ਦੁਖੀ ਦੁਸਟ ਦੁਬਾਜਰਾ ਸੁਤਰ ਮੁਰਗ ਹੋਇ ਕੰਮਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: dhukhee dhusaT dhubaajaraa sutar murag hoi ka(n)m na aavai|

en.bdb: The evil person who is double-talker is always unhappy and is useless like an ostrich.

verses.gurmukhi: ਉਡਣਿ ਉਡੈ ਨ ਲਦੀਐ ਪੁਰਸੁਸ ਹੋਈ ਆਪੁ ਲਖਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: auddan uddai na ladheeaai purasus hoiee aap lakhaavai|

en.bdb: An ostrich can neither fly nor can be laden, but it strutts ostentatiously.

verses.gurmukhi: ਹਸਤੀ ਦੰਦ ਵਖਾਣੀਅਨਿ ਹੋਰੁ ਦਿਖਾਲੈ ਹੋਰਤੁ ਖਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: hasatee dha(n)dh vakhaaneean hor dhikhaalai horat khaavai|

en.bdb: The elephant has one set of teeth for display and another for eating.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬਕਰੀਆਂ ਨੋ ਚਾਰ ਥਣ ਦੁਇ ਗਲ ਵਿਚਿ ਦੁਇ ਲੇਵੈ ਲਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: bakareeaa(n) no chaar than dhui gal vich dhui levai laavai|

en.bdb: Goats have four teats, two on their necks and two attached to their udders.

verses.gurmukhi: ਇਕਨੀ ਦੁਧੁ ਸਮਾਵਦਾ ਇਕ ਠਗਾਊ ਠਗ ਠਗਾਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: eikanee dhudh samaavadhaa ik Thagaauoo Thag Thagaavai|

en.bdb: The latter contain milk, the former deceive those who expect milk from them.

verses.gurmukhi: ਮੋਰਾਂ ਅਖੀ ਚਾਰਿ ਚਾਰਿ ਉਇ ਦੇਖਨਿ ਓਨੀ ਦਿਸਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ।
verses.translit_en: moraa(n) akhee chaar chaar ui dhekhan onee dhis na aavai|

en.bdb: Peacocks have four eyes through which they behold but others know nothing about them.
So turning one's attention to two masters (religions) leads to disastrous failure.
